annotations.text:
A · FORM STRIP
The 20-game window becomes one object you read in a glance: colour = result, bar height = souls/min that game. The match list survives as a hover.

Tradeoff: no hero or KDA visible until you hover. Scanning "which game was the Lash one" gets slower.

B · COACH-FIRST
Leads with a diagnosis, then the numbers that justify it. Most true to "coaching-first, not a stats dashboard". Matches demoted to a thin rail.

Tradeoff: lives or dies on the headline being right. If the claim is obvious or wrong, the whole page feels hollow — and it needs a real cross-match pattern engine, not just the per-match diff we have.

C · COMMAND CENTER
Sidebar shell, rings comparing this window to your own median, one big switchable trend chart. The most conventional "app dashboard" of the four.

Tradeoff: it's also the most like every other tracker — the thing Vantage is trying not to be. Densest to read.

D · MATCH SPOTLIGHT
Keeps matches central but stops being a table: the last game gets a full card with its verdict and economy curve already on it, older games become cards with one insight each.

Tradeoff: only ~5 games fit before scrolling, and it repeats what the Review tab already shows.

Four answers to the same question: where do the matches go?
All four use Vantage's real tokens (Sora/Inter, #0b0c10 ground, #f0a020 accent) and your real data from the last 20 games.
Static mockups — nothing clickable yet.
